segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Dana. I saw your note about expanding the analytics workspace from 32 to 45 seats before the October rollout. Is that still the count you want to plan around?

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: It is, yeah. We have 12 customer success managers starting October 14, plus one operations lead. So 45 total, but I want the invoice to reflect the increase starting November 1 if possible.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: That works. Your current term runs through March 31, and adding 13 seats on November 1 would prorate the remaining five months. On the pricing sheet, that comes to $7,475 for the add-on period.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay, that is about what I expected. Can you keep it on net 30? Our AP team gets picky if a mid-term add-on has different payment terms.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, same net 30 terms, same billing contact, and it will reference the existing agreement number. No change to the renewal date.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Good. The only other thing is provisioning. We need the new users able to log in by October 10 so managers can build their dashboards before training.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Understood. If we have the signed order by October 4, implementation can open the seats on October 8. That gives you a couple days of buffer before the 10th.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That timeline is fine. Send it to me and copy Marcus in procurement. He does not need a call, he just wants the order form and the tax breakdown.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. I’ll send the order form today with 13 additional seats, November 1 billing start, net 30, and the $7,475 prorated total. Marcus will be copied.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. If it matches that, I can sign tomorrow morning.
